prior_art_found.source: Separating signal from noise in wastewater data: An algorithm to identify community-level COVID-19 surges in real time (PNAS 2023)
prior_art_found.snippet: Wastewater monitoring has provided health officials with early warnings for new COVID-19 outbreaks, but to date, no approach has been validated to distinguish signal (sustained surges) from noise (background variability) in wastewater data... The Covid-SURGE algorithm reliably distinguishes signal from noise in the wastewater data, flags community-level surges, and gives public health officials a timely way to assess the need for heightened response.
prior_art_found.relevance: Directly targets the niche's 'rising?/real?/what action?' question, but is a deterministic multi-metric rule-based algorithm, NOT a learned test-time-adaptive anomaly detector. No FPM/TTA mechanism.

results.exact_unused_slice: Curated test-time adaptation (unlabeled, online) with False-Positive Mining + spatiotemporally-aware normality adaptation applied to multivariate wastewater viral-surveillance SIGNAL INTERPRETATION (is the rise real vs a shedding/population/sampling artifact), treating time-varying shedding rates and sewershed-population remapping as the distribution shift to adapt to at inference. No source applies a TTA/FPM anomaly detector to this surveillance-interpretation task.
results.honest_adjacency: Heavy adjacency on the NICHE axis: the 'separate signal from noise / is this surge real' problem is explicitly named and addressed by the Covid-SURGE rule-based algorithm and by NWSS/Biobot normalization+percentile analytics. Strong adjacency on the TECHNIQUE axis within wastewater: domain adaptation for anomalous effluent-quality fluctuations, cross-sewershed transfer learning, and lifelong-learning LSTMs explicitly motivated by wastewater distribution shift. What is NOT present is the specific intersection: test-time (inference-time, unlabeled) adaptation with curated false-positive mining for the viral-surveillance multivariate anomaly/signal-validity task.
results.reasoning: Both axes are well populated independently and there is even a domain-adaptation-for-anomaly paper inside wastewater (treatment-plant effluent), so this is clearly not OPEN. But no deployed product or paper combines test-time adaptation / FPM-style curated adaptation with the viral-RNA surveillance signal-interpretation task; existing surveillance interpretation is rule/percentile-based and existing wastewater ML is forecasting or treatment-process anomaly detection. The shedding-rate and sewershed-population variability framing maps cleanly onto CANDI's distribution-shift motivation, making the gap real but narrow rather than wide-open. Verdict NARROW.

results.honest_adjacency: Strong adjacency on BOTH axes. Technique axis: agentic/multi-agent graph RAG already applied to commercial contracts and capital-markets queries, and KG-based conflict resolution (TruthfulRAG, DRAGged-into-Conflicts) handles exactly 'contradictory terms' on sibling document types; financial event-extraction-into-KG (FinKario, equity repurchase/freeze events) is corporate-action-adjacent. What is missing is the specific union: multi-agent graph RAG for contradictory-offering-doc reconciliation and elective-event decisioning.
results.reasoning: Cannot be CLOSED: vendor AI for corporate actions centers on reconciliation/matching/exceptions and ISO message tagging, and the academic graph-RAG conflict-resolution work is on legal/contract/generic siblings, not corporate-action elections; no deployed or published system reconciles contradictory offering-doc terms into elective-event decisions via multi-agent graph RAG. Cannot be OPEN: the technique-family is demonstrably applied to neighboring financial/legal documents (commercial contracts, capital markets, financial event KGs) and the niche is an active commercial-automation target, so adjacency exists on both axes within one reformulation.
